## 1. Scope and Source Posture

### 1.1 Authority, purpose, and authorization

**TCR-REQ-001 — Scoped authority.** This handoff MUST be the authoritative
change plan for the test-suite rationalization effort described here. Its
requirements govern consolidation decisions, preservation obligations, evidence,
sequencing, and completion. Adopted subsystem NLSpecs and normative Core sections
MUST continue to govern production behavior under
[Core 00 precedence](../spec/00_document_set_status_and_precedence.md).
The [Testing Harness NLSpec](../testing-harness-nlspec.md) MUST govern harness
semantics. This handoff MUST NOT override either authority, declare a new product
requirement, or promote an implementation observation into a requirement.

The [NLSpec grounding document](../research/nlspec-spec.md) supplies writing
discipline. The [modular refactor framework](cartulary_modular_refactor_planning_framework.md)
supplies planning doctrine. Neither establishes that a test, defect, or runtime
result exists. The [domain document](../domain.md) supplies vocabulary and owner
navigation; it does not establish exact test selectors or internal filenames.

**TCR-REQ-002 — Current authorization.** On 2026-11-10 the maintainer explicitly
requested implementation of the expanded specification and test-consolidation
remediation plan. This supersedes the earlier document-only invocation, whose
evidence remains historical. Authorized work includes S-065, S-059–S-063,
S-066–S-073, a fresh semantic review of every owner and assertion, the separately
recorded corrections needed to close confirmed gaps, targeted qualification,
and final S-064 validation/handoff. No staging, commit, merge or deployment is
requested.

On 2026-11-11 the maintainer requested a graceful stopping point for a future
restart. Execution stops after completing and qualifying S-342. Resume the
partial A-module.imports review only after a new continuation request; the pause
does not close that owner, any remaining owner, or S-064. The restart checkpoint
below records completed review, pending inspection, and the next correction.

On 2026-11-12 the maintainer explicitly resumed implementation at S-343,
continuing all remaining owners lexically and S-064 last. The pause is lifted;
its completed review and compatible qualification remain preserved history.

On 2026-11-14 the maintainer requested a graceful stopping point and a commit of
the accumulated work. Finish and qualify S-641, record the restart checkpoint,
and pause before the next slice. This request authorizes staging and committing
the accumulated remediation changes, superseding the earlier no-stage/no-commit
restriction for this checkpoint. It does not authorize publication or close the
remaining owners or S-064.

Execute the §6 schedule sequentially. Update this tracker after completing each
workstream and before beginning the next. Qualify successors before retiring
predecessors. Record an adopted-contract production defect as a separate
owner-backed corrective slice before repair; this implementation request covers
necessary corrections within the testing seam. A substantive new requirement
still needs primary-owner adoption before dependent implementation. Defective
behavior is not a compatibility promise. Existing behavior must have an adopted
requirement or explicit engineering purpose, not merely historical presence.

**TCR-REQ-003 — Prose isolation.** Tests, generators, runtime metadata,
conformance, and release evidence MUST NOT read, stat, hash, parse, or depend on
this handoff, other Cartulary specification/adoption prose, `docs/`, or
README. The mappings below are human review records. They MUST NOT become a new
executable requirement registry. Existing canonical artifacts and machine-readable
expectations remain executable inputs. Offline source producers retain only the
pinned-upstream exception already allowed by repository procedure.

### 1.2 Target, scope, and evidence vocabulary

The supplied repository root is `/home/jochi/code/cartulary`; the canonical
repository-relative target is `.`. The target kind is a cross-repository
testing seam, not a new production module. The label is `test-consolidation`.
The controlling artifact is `docs/handoffs/test-consolidation-refactor-tracker.md`.
Its ancestors are ordinary directories; it is a regular, singly linked file.
The original absent-output admission remains in the historical baseline.

The historical portfolio includes all discoverable test responsibilities: product,
architecture, security, harness infrastructure, tooling, documentation tooling,
producer, development-only, generated projections, and vendored tests. Current
implementation includes continuation/merge consolidation, named deferred SQL,
lifecycle, extension/clock, administrative-audit and evidence-class reviews,
cost/reliability disposition, and every owner's assertion-level semantic audit.
The entry catalog contains 2,613 rows across 66 owners; rows are not assertion
counts. Runtime qualification covers affected tests and assertion successors,
not an unconditional whole-suite rerun. There is no required speed improvement.
Unrelated product redesign, unsupported platform expansion and unrelated cleanup
remain outside this effort; no public API or data migration is presently planned.

**TCR-REQ-004 — Evidence semantics.** Each assertion in this tracker MUST be
identified by its role:

| Role | Meaning | Permitted conclusion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Normative requirement | A TCR requirement or an explicitly referenced adopted owner clause. | Determines required behavior within its authority. |
| Confirmed static observation | Supported by inspected source at the recorded baseline. | Establishes source structure or an assertion's actual scope; does not establish a runtime pass. |
| Inference / potential concern | Plausible consequence not established by runtime or complete semantic evidence. | Opens bounded investigation; does not permit removal. |
| Unresolved evidence | A named missing fact, artifact, owner decision, or characterization. | Blocks the dependent decision. |
| Rationale | Explanation of a decision. | Supports understanding; adds no requirement. |

Work status is exactly `TODO`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `BLOCKED`,
`DONE`, `DEFERRED`, or `DROPPED`. Finding classification is
exactly `must_fix`, `should_fix`, `defer`, or
`intentional/no_action`. Planning completeness, readiness, and authorization
are separate outcome fields. A planning item marked DONE MUST NOT imply that
its future implementation is complete.

Missing duration, resource, retry, or execution evidence defaults to
`unmeasured` or `not executed`, never zero, stable, or passed.
Missing authority defaults to `unresolved`, never unnecessary. An
unreviewed test defaults to `retain pending evidence`.

## 2. Current-State Repository Inventory

### 2.1 Inventory contract and coverage boundary

**TCR-REQ-006 — Complete accounting.** Inventory closure MUST reconcile four
sets: source-defined tests and registrations; supporting files and fixtures;
canonical catalog selections; and public/non-public execution entrypoints.
Filename conventions alone MUST NOT define the universe. TestMain, benchmarks,
fuzz targets, parameterized cases, registration modules, shell entrypoints,
generator checks, and tests excluded from canonical discovery MUST receive an
explicit disposition.

The original planning baseline enumerated all tracked/non-ignored paths and all
`tools/test_families/*.json` rows. Named-file accounting below is
metadata-only except where E-IDs identify direct inspection. Family metadata
was inspected for all 66 owners. Detailed assertion inspection is limited to
the named candidate groups and counterparts in Sections 4, 5, and 10.
The original unresolved registrations are closed by S-001 and the current
disposition delta in §2.5. Complete source/catalog accounting is established;
exhaustive product requirement coverage and full-suite runtime acceptance are
separate and are not claimed.

Generated output, fixture data, ignored caches, installed dependencies, and
vendored code MUST remain visible as separate accounting classes. They MUST NOT
be counted as authored runnable tests merely because they contain test-like
names. Symbolic links and submodules MUST be recorded without following external
targets. Ignored installed dependencies and retained result trees are excluded
from authored-test enumeration; explicitly selected historical artifacts may be
inspected only through the owning observation procedure.

**TCR-REQ-007 — Responsibility classification.** Each reviewed test or coherent
test group MUST record its actual assertion purpose separately from catalog
owner, behavior class, runner, evidence class, aggregate placement, and fixture
capability. Product, architecture, security, harness, tooling, documentation,
producer, development-only, and vendor responsibilities MAY coexist within a
group; the group MUST be split for decision accounting when those obligations
would otherwise be lost. Supporting classification MUST NOT imply low value.

### 2.4 Review record and registration reconciliation

**TCR-REQ-008 — Review interface.** Each future reviewed group MUST have a
documented record containing the fields below. A shared record MAY cover cases
only when their obligation, scope, profile, and disposition are identical.

| Field | Required meaning / default |
| --- | --- |
| Identity | Source path, test identifier or registration, parameterized case boundaries, current catalog row IDs or explicit uncatalogued status. |
| Responsibility | Actual assertion purpose; primary owner and collaborators; declared classification separately. |
| Contract | Requirement/acceptance references where established; otherwise explicit engineering purpose and owner. Absence of a clause is not a removal reason. |
| Implementation | Production or supporting path and interface actually exercised; mock, fixture, HTTP, process, browser, or static scope. |
| Assertion | Preconditions, stimulus, observable result, failure oracle, and relevant negative/edge cases. |
| Selection | Public Make selector, runner/project, runtime and fixture profiles, aggregate placement, isolation, and service dependencies. |
| Evidence | Baseline, inspection depth, exact execution command/environment/result/artifact when available; otherwise not executed. |
| Cost and reliability | Setup/execution/cleanup, resource and contention observations, retries/failures, measurement limits; default unmeasured. |
| Disposition | retain, consolidate, relocate, correct, investigate, or retire; retain pending evidence is the default. |
| Traceability | Finding, contract, slice, validation, blockers, and completion evidence IDs. |

#### Execution registration reconciliation

At beaf0293634e6aef9e62aa5670e033a26b6458d3, source and registration inspection
accounts for 2,086 test-shaped or nonconventional registration files. This extends
the original 2,083-name census with three registration modules, not three newly
added tests. The canonical catalog remains 2,611 rows across 66 owners.
`make source-check CHECK=catalog` passed under run ID
`tcr-s001-catalog-20261109-01` (outer exit 0); its exact retained root is
`.cartulary/test-results/tcr-s001-catalog-20261109-01`. This validates current
catalog/source closure, not the correctness or completeness of product assertions.

All 1,321 Go test files and 612 frontend test/spec files have accountable catalog
package/file ownership. A separate declaration inspection found no unmatched
ordinary Go Test declaration or frontend file. The 282 Go files without an
ordinary Test declaration are retained package helpers/setup; filename count is
not a count of assertions. There are three TestMain entrypoints: serverprocess
owns service setup/cleanup; processtest owns bounded subprocess fixtures; ATT&CK
producer owns test-only CLI child dispatch. None is an independent catalog test.
The single FuzzTimeBucketArithmetic context remains development-only; ordinary
TestTimeBucketArithmeticPropertySeeds_Unit supplies selected deterministic
arithmetic coverage. No Benchmark declaration was found in this source posture.
Linux-constrained helper tests remain in the current Linux/WSL execution context;
this does not qualify another operating system.

Node/shell discovery separately inspected registration imports and exported
registration functions, including initialization-tests.mjs,
contract-initialization-cases.mjs and run-observation-cases.mjs. Every registration
candidate has an authored operation or registrar reference. Source references are
not execution passes. Test-output and catalog implementation helpers are not
miscounted as assertions. Ten vendored Python files retain upstream development
assurance and are deliberately outside canonical product discovery. They are not
executed, copied into product runners, or credited as product conformance.

The inventory below is registration-level inspection with explicit retention
purpose; it does not claim every assertion has received deep semantic review.
Named candidate assertions have the deeper inspection recorded in E-004–E-016.
S-011 and S-012 own semantic classification, obligation gaps and runtime evidence.
Fixture data and other supporting sources remain accounted by their authored
support/fixture inventories and the original whole-repository enumeration; they
are not independently runnable tests. No inventory entry is retired by this slice.

## 3. Module Boundary Diagnosis

### 3.1 Structural diagnosis

The testing ecosystem is a cross-owner assurance system. It MUST NOT be treated
as one production module. Central source-policy enforcement, local architectural
assertions, tests of checker mechanics, assembled product witnesses, and
browser choreography hide different decisions. Shared machinery is justified
only when it preserves those distinctions.

| Responsibility found | Current location | Owner candidate | Disposition | Evidence / finding / contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Production test-support and generated-contract import isolation | codegenboundary Go tests. | Existing harness.generated_artifacts and module.revisions selection owners. | Correct scanner first; consolidate subset only after effective survivor/routing proof. | E-004; F-001/F-002; C-002. |
| Package capability and import topology policies | Local module guards plus backend JSON/checker. | Semantic module policy owners; harness owns mechanics. | Consolidate overlapping mechanics after policy equivalence; unresolved file/package authority deferred. | E-005–E-007; F-003/F-004; C-003. |
| Projection SQL and descriptor consistency | projectionassembly tests, central SQL parser/policy. | module.projections; harness parser owner. | Separate reusable parsing from descriptor/source-authority obligations. | E-008; F-005; C-004. |
| Frontend dependency and semantic capability boundaries | Local Vitest guards and frontend policy. | web.architecture, web.workbook, module.imports and relevant owners. | Consolidate identical dependency rules; preserve distinct symbol/type/transport checks. | E-009; F-006/F-007; C-005. |

### 3.2 Consolidation decision protocol

**TCR-REQ-009 — Retirement gate.** Removal or relocation MUST preserve every
active obligation of the original case, including useful engineering assurance
without an explicit product clause. Before retirement, the change record MUST
identify the original assertion, required behavior or engineering purpose,
surviving assertion, implementation boundary, execution scope and exemptions,
runtime/fixture profiles, owner selection, and compatible validation evidence.
A stricter name, larger suite, shared helper, or passing replacement label is
insufficient.

**TCR-REQ-010 — Decision algorithm.** A candidate MUST be evaluated in this order:

1. Establish its owner-required behavior or engineering purpose and actual
   assertion scope.
2. Separate ineffective or contradictory expectations from valid obligations.
   Correctness changes MUST be tracked separately from structural movement.
3. Identify the survivor for each valid obligation; preserve any unmatched
   obligation in the original or a separately characterized test.
4. Compare input/failure cases, observable outcomes, scopes, exemptions, execution
   boundaries, profiles, and owner selection.
5. Establish effectiveness with relevant negative and allowed-transformation
   fixtures, plus compatible runtime evidence where runtime behavior is claimed.
6. Update authored selection/accounting inputs atomically with any retirement;
   use canonical generation only during authorized implementation.
7. Retire only when every preservation and validation gate is satisfied.
   Otherwise retain and record the missing evidence.

Retirement for an obsolete purpose MUST identify the adopted owner decision or
bounded engineering-owner justification that ended that purpose. Mere absence
of a normative reference MUST NOT satisfy that condition. Independent process,
browser, order, security, or failure-cleanup evidence MUST remain distinct when
a lower layer cannot observe its boundary.

**Rationale — non-normative.** The primary structural burden is duplicated
policy maintenance and mismatched execution boundaries. Reducing test count
without establishing effective surviving assertions would worsen assurance.

qualified. No broad compatibility wrapper, mutable shared fixture, retired-row
alias, test-count target or production architecture change is proposed.

### 5.2 Architectural preservation requirements

**TCR-REQ-012 — Effective guards.** Source-policy checks MUST prove that their
intended roots are selected. Empty selection MUST fail where production source
is required. Negative fixtures MUST prove the forbidden construct reaches the
detector. Allowed rename/split, alias, quote, and support-exemption fixtures MUST
remain accepted when the adopted policy permits them. The scanner correction
MUST NOT silently widen or narrow dependency policy.

**TCR-REQ-013 — Backend equivalence.** Consolidation MUST compare root-only
versus recursive scope, exact versus subtree imports, package versus file grants,
generated/support/test exclusions, and build-constraint treatment. Checker
mechanics/CLI tests MUST NOT be removed as duplicates of production-source
checks. The broad testutil ban MUST NOT be replaced solely by the pgtest ban.
The SQLC export check MUST retain rejection of generated SQL types in the
exported declaration forms it currently inspects; a dependency allowlist alone
does not supply this guarantee.

**TCR-REQ-014 — Projection preservation.** SQL parsing consolidation MUST retain
both relation access enforcement and provider-declared source authority. Active
descriptor, boundary-policy, recovery, and migration table sets MUST continue to
agree. Tests MUST distinguish reads, writes, and locks; qualify quoted/schema
names and CTEs; and demonstrate that an extracted/new SQL-bearing provider source
does not escape review. Existing test-support delegation to production assembly
and protected exported surfaces MUST retain their own evidence.

**TCR-REQ-015 — Frontend preservation.** Moving dependency checks MUST preserve
resolution of aliases, namespace imports, re-exports, dynamic imports, and
type-only distinctions where relevant to the rule. Ambient fetch detection,
complete source ownership, semantic grid focus/geometry, privileged capability
typing, and Network Flow browser-evidence/design-token restrictions MUST remain
separate obligations unless an equivalent surviving check demonstrably covers
them. Literal source-spelling assertions MUST NOT be replaced by import presence
alone when the intended obligation is actual claim-gated behavior.

### 5.3 Browser probe mapping

**TCR-REQ-016 — Browser relocation boundary.** A `page.request` assertion
MUST be credited for the API boundary actually exercised. Manual CSRF header
construction MUST NOT be credited as UI-client submission, negative CSRF,
cookie-policy, or CORS evidence. API fixture setup or post-UI persistence checks
MUST NOT be classified as redundant merely because they use requests.

files. The 18 catalog rows in browser-support families include real keyboard,
paste/fill, grouping, virtualization, and pending-navigation observations.
Those rows MUST NOT be retired as a class.

### 5.4 Stability, burden, and coverage requirements

**TCR-REQ-017 — Reliability evidence.** A flaky classification MUST distinguish
observed inconsistent outcomes under materially equivalent inputs from a
potential timing/shared-state concern. Records MUST identify source/profile,
exact command, attempts, failure signatures, and environmental differences.
A pass after retry MUST NOT erase the original failure. This handoff MUST NOT
authorize blind reruns, increased timeouts, service resets, or relaxed assertions.

**TCR-REQ-018 — Cost evidence.** Investigation MUST distinguish setup, test-body,
cleanup, shared-service, resource-admission, and critical-path costs. Evidence
MUST identify exact selected rows/cases, source, profiles, environment, cache
mode, and measurement limits. Removing an assertion within an existing browser
scenario MUST NOT be claimed to remove browser-stack startup cost. Reducing
full-tier rows MUST NOT be claimed to accelerate the fast gate. No percentage,
duration target, or harness performance qualification gate is introduced.

**TCR-REQ-019 — Supporting assurance.** Supporting tests MUST be evaluated by
the failure they detect and the boundary they prove. Required smoke roles,
generated drift/policy, migration integrity, product/static/security checks,
runtime admission/reset contracts, full-tier self-regressions, and explicit-only
UI-review/visual obligations MUST follow the adopted harness placement rules.
A test MUST NOT be moved solely to improve a reported gate duration.

**TCR-REQ-020 — Coverage gaps.** Each identified owner requirement without
established test evidence MUST record the required observation, existing partial
coverage, missing scenario, responsible owner, and blocking decision. Tests with
no explicit requirement MUST record their engineering purpose rather than be
discarded. Existing evidence that contradicts the primary owner MUST be
classified as characterization or negative evidence until separately corrected.
The five-command harness restatement MUST NOT override Core's seven commands.

backend gate now accepts every affected production query without an unresolved

  Literal relations and token-separated fragments prevent arbitrary construction.

  Restore insertion excludes derived storage; protected metadata/control tables
  retain distinct operations. Generated SQL stays in ordinary ownership scans.

  parameters instead of generated placeholder lists; ordering/results are retained.

- The final permission audit replaced six remaining Reporting production SQL

- Core 01 and the Harness NLSpec distinguish frozen-catalog physical maintenance

  records construction limits, provider/shared-reader admission, removed internal
  paths and migration notes. No public API, schema, stored-data or deployment
  migration is required.

### 8.1 Validation interface and canonical commands

**TCR-REQ-022 — Validation boundaries.** Future validation MUST use public Make
targets from the repository root and current test-operations guidance.
Selection/plan success MUST NOT count as execution success. Each slice MUST
select the smallest checks covering changed behavior and directly affected
dependencies, then stop when those checks and their declared cleanup pass.
Broader execution requires a concrete uncovered risk or an explicit broader
acceptance request. Complete-effort accounting MUST compare compatible evidence
without treating that accounting as permission to rerun complete owners.
Explicit-only, process/order, security, and measurement obligations MUST remain
explicit when the requested acceptance scope includes them. Generation and
finalization MUST be conditional on actual affected outputs or requested
maintenance; an implementation edit alone does not require them.

Each invocation record MUST contain its exact resolved command, fresh
literal run identity, source baseline, selected rows/cases, runtime/fixture
profiles, environment, outer exit, terminal result, artifact path, and remaining
applicability limits. Product execution requires an authorized implementation task;
current TCR-REQ-002 authorizes the expanded implementation and targeted checks.

- Continuation's changed workload has a lower observed graph and grouped-runner
  duration. It replaces twelve deep scenarios with twelve small ones and therefore
  is not a controlled equivalent-work performance comparison. Build time also
  differs: report-renderer 35897 versus 24897 ms, server-harness 27219 versus
  27490 ms. Single samples, shared build caches and unmeasured host load prevent
  causal speedup or stability claims. Merge observations are similar; SQL's
  consolidated fixture run is longer in this sample. Neither establishes a
  regression, improvement, or confidence interval.
- Phase unions overlap (117/131 ms for the continuation runs); they are not
  additive totals. Selected cleanup also includes phases outside fixture release.
  Canonical graph wall excludes portions of Make/preflight, final scanning and
  return/publication accounting. It is not full user-perceived command latency.
- Invocation-path queue is 0–2 ms in these samples. This is evidence of little
  recorded scheduler waiting in these invocations, not absence of machine,
  database, filesystem or external contention. Cache lookup/publication phases
  do not measure compiler, OS or browser cache effects.
- Only the two continuation runs used basic resource diagnostics. Both report
  complete collection with observed-partial coverage (764 and 553 samples), not
  complete process attribution; bounded explanations omit 36 and 45 scopes.
  Sampling misses short-lived processes, reservations are not consumption, and
  guest observations do not represent Windows-host usage. Instrumentation itself
  consumes resources; no uninstrumented control or subtraction was performed.
  Other runs report resource observation off, so their CPU/RSS cost is unknown.
- All targeted qualification runs in this effort passed with completed cleanup
  and passing retained-secret scans; no test failure or retry requires a new
  failure disposition. S-067 format's outer native exit was not retained across
  context turnover; its passing terminal summary is recorded with that explicit
  limitation and is not upgraded to an independently observed native exit.
  These facts do not establish whole-suite stability or a failure-rate estimate.

Decision: retain the structural remediation already justified by assertion
ownership; do not add timeout changes, shared-state shortcuts, a cache layer,
resource accounting mandate, timing gates, host changes or speculative fixture
optimization. No additional runtime was necessary for this descriptive analysis.
F-014 is closed as an evidence disposition, with marginal performance and global
stability explicitly unmeasured. There is no compatibility or migration impact.
The risk of overstating a single-run delta is addressed by the limitations above;
future performance work requires a specific hypothesis and compatible repeated
observations. `make lint-markdown` and `git diff --check` close this documentation
checkpoint. V-030 is satisfied; lexical owner audits can begin. S-064 remains
blocked on all owner audits and their corrective slices.

### S-080 — Lease-test failure-path ownership (DONE / E-062)

F-071: the real PostgreSQL application-lease test releases its handles only on
the success path, and both lease integration tests discard a returned handle
when expecting acquisition rejection. A regression causing an early assertion
failure or unexpected successful acquisition can retain a checked-out connection
while `pool.Close` waits, obscuring the primary failure with a timeout. The actual
lease and PostgreSQL adapter were read: `Close` is idempotent, stops monitoring
and disposes the exact session; pool ownership alone cannot release that borrow.

Remediation: register cleanup immediately for every acquired lease, including
unexpected contender handles, while retaining explicit release/crash observations.
Areas: tests and tracker. Engineering purpose/benefit: failure diagnostics settle
their resources as reliably as successful tests; no shared cleanup framework or
lease semantics change. Compatibility/migration: none. Risk unresolved: hung pool
cleanup and lost primary diagnostics on precisely the failures these tests seek.
Entry: S-079 closed; both integration bodies and real lifecycle implementation
reviewed. Exit: both exact existing integration rows pass with registered cleanup
in reverse acquisition order. S-064 depends on S-080; A-app.server remains open.

### S-081 — Profile-lock test settlement (DONE / E-063)

F-072: the logical state-store timeout test waits unconditionally for a holder's
acquisition signal and releases that holder only after the assertion passes. An
acquisition error never signals readiness, and a failed timeout assertion leaves
the holder blocked while pool cleanup waits. This is a test-lifetime defect in the
adapter witness, independent of the production lock-timeout mapping.

Remediation: make the holder cancellable, register settlement before waiting,
observe acquisition failure as well as readiness, and bound readiness/settlement
waits. Keep the real PostgreSQL contention and exact logical timeout error. Areas:
tests and tracker. Benefit: preserve useful primary failures and prevent a test
coordination deadlock without changing lock policy or introducing shared fixtures.
Compatibility/migration: none. Risk unresolved: an adapter regression becomes a
suite timeout instead of a local diagnostic. Entry: S-080 closed; logical adapter
and physical lock acquisition/release inspected. Exit: existing two-test adapter
row passes, holder cleanup precedes pool cleanup and propagates holder errors.
S-064 depends on S-081; A-app.server remains in progress.

or production timeout changes. Cleanup cancels the holder and checks its error
before pool cleanup, even when the contention assertion fails. Exact logical
timeout mapping, capability scope, negative capability exposure, rollback and

acquisition owns its cleanup independently of every caller's success path.

explicit early Stop remains valid; no product/API/storage migration. Risk if
unresolved: hanging negative tests can contaminate later runs with owned child

### S-086 — Exercise manifest privacy with present secret inputs (DONE / E-069)

F-077: the worker-manifest test replaces its password with numeric 42, then
asserts two unrelated string passwords are absent from that error. Neither string
is in that failing input. Its duplicate-user test contains both passwords but
checks only a diagnostic substring, so echoed passwords would pass. The parser
already produces safe diagnostics; this is an ineffective privacy witness.

Remediation: retain valid/schema/type/duplicate predicates in the existing test,
while capturing each failed parse and checking its expected reason plus absence
of secret markers actually present in that input. Include malformed JSON, a
structural error and duplicate identity with secret-bearing entries; keep invalid
password-type rejection independently. Areas: tests/documentation only. Governing
purpose: Harness private-state and safe diagnostic boundaries. Benefit: future
parser exceptions or diagnostic interpolation cannot silently expose manifest
credentials. Compatibility/migration: no parser/selector/schema/profile/API
change. Risk unresolved: privacy regression passes a vacuous negative assertion.
Change risk: conflating structural validation with privacy; preserve separate
reason checks and literal present-input markers.

Entry: complete parser and caller test read; no runtime leak discovered. Exit:
exact private-state harness-node row passes all retained and new cases, native
exit/terminal scan/cleanup recorded, Markdown and diff checks pass. No generated
input or product runtime change; no browser, golden or broad rerun required.
S-064 depends on S-086; A-harness.browser remains in progress.

### F-078 / S-087 — Remove unowned browser-state fallbacks (queued correction)

A-harness.browser found that `harnessState` can resolve credential-state files
into process-global temporary paths, eagerly resolves those paths at import in
worker/suite admin helpers, and creates a configured directory with ambient
permissions. `verifyOwnedHarnessRuntime` reports success without a token. Current
Playwright configuration already requires a Make-owned validated attachment and
one owned worker; these older fallback branches add no supported execution mode.
Harness private-runtime requirements (following TH-HARNESS-REQ-603) require exact
owned private namespaces and safe consumers. Existing canonical startup creates
the private state directory and validates the native owner marker; preserve and
reuse that authority rather than inventing a second owner or repairing modes.

Required remediation direction: one explicit owned-state boundary, lazy pure
imports, no global temporary credential fallback or identity-check bypass, and
safe private reads/writes/cleanup using the existing native/runtime file boundary.
Retire obsolete local-mode branches and unused context inputs where callers no
longer need them. Tests must independently prove missing/wrong ownership and
binding rejection, privacy, isolation, valid owned state and lifecycle. Preserve
canonical shared-stack lifetime and single-worker reuse. No compatibility alias
or migration of old global temporary secret files; leave unowned files untouched.
Areas: harness implementation, support tests/routing as necessary, documentation.
Benefit: one explicit resource owner and fail-closed setup; risk unresolved is
cross-run credential state or silently skipped runtime identity proof. Change
risks are import-time side effects, cleanup ordering and binding the wrong native
suite lifetime; inspect existing browser attachment/native facades before choosing
an implementation. S-087 is queued, not implemented or qualified. Exact targeted
selection and final implementation entry gates will be recorded before mutation.
S-064 and A-harness.browser closure depend on this correction.

admission to isolate adapter rejection, then a real owned browser fixture will

for obsolete modes change without aliases; existing row identities remain.

### F-081 / S-090 — Fence normalized test-control paths (queued)

The complete `testControlClient.test.ts` and client read confirms a boundary gap:
its traversal-rejection title contains only public/absolute/network-path inputs;
`requireControlPath` checks the raw `/api/v1/test/` prefix, then normalizes with
`URL` without rechecking the resulting pathname. A dot-segment path can therefore
send the privileged header to a public route on the approved origin. Exact-origin
checks and private token serialization remain useful and must survive.

Remediate at the test-control transport boundary: reject ambiguous/traversing paths
before dispatch, including normalized and encoded dot-segment/backslash cases;
retain exact approved origin and genuine test-route requests. Establish the
adopted Harness/Core test-route authority clause before implementation. Areas:
harness support/tests/documentation, with routing changes only if case identities
change. Benefit: privileged requests stay within their intended API namespace.
No product migration or compatibility alias for invalid paths. Unresolved risk:
helper accepts a request its existing test title claims to prohibit. Exit: a
nonvacuous negative matrix observes zero dispatches and no token disclosure, valid
control requests retain exact bytes/headers, and the exact transport row passes.
S-090 follows queued S-088/S-089; A-harness.browser and S-064 depend on it. No
implementation or new runtime evidence is claimed yet.

### S-088 implementation entry — owned authentication request lifetimes

S-087 checkpoint is closed. Adjacent caller review confirms the same finally-
replacement problem in transient suite-admin, worker-login, revocation-verification
and password-probe contexts. Bootstrap control-plane acquisition also creates the
returned context before disposing its anonymous predecessor: failed predecessor
cleanup can prevent transfer and strand the new context.

Use one small authentication request-lifetime helper, with an explicit owned
context, operation and optional retirement action; always attempt disposal after
retirement failure and preserve operation versus cleanup failures separately.
Borrowed contexts continue using their owner's lifetime. Construct the returned
bootstrap context only after the anonymous predecessor has completed its lifetime.
This is private test support, not a general fixture framework or product change.
Native stack ownership still covers bootstrap server state if setup fails before
an authenticated context can transfer. Tests exercise operation/retirement/disposal
failures, ordering, exactly-once releases, returned values and simultaneous failures;
add cases to the existing sessions support row. Qualify that row, the affected
suite-admin identity row, typed consumers and one real fixture-state browser row.
Regenerate title projections and check generated/catalog, then update this checkpoint
before S-089. No broader owner, visual, release or performance acceptance is needed.

### F-082 / S-091 — Keep workbook observation within the requested surface (queued)

The Timeline test-support review confirms that `workbookGridScope(container,
surface)` falls back to the entire container when that surface's grid is absent.
`visibleGridRowRecordIds(container, surface)` can then return matching rows from
another surface. The wrong-surface test always mounts an empty Timeline shell,
so it does not exercise the absent-shell fallback. Global `screen` shell waits
also need reconciliation with the caller's supplied container.

Remediate this observation boundary structurally: an explicitly selected surface
never widens to its container; absent readiness yields empty observations or the
existing bounded readiness failure. Scope shell/control acquisition to the same
container. Areas: test support/tests/documentation. No product or public API/data
migration; inspect callers for any reliance on the invalid fallback and migrate
them together. Benefit: readiness cannot be satisfied by unrelated mounted UI.
Risk unresolved: false-positive identity readiness or wrong returned grid when
multiple containers/surfaces exist. Exit: literal wrong/missing-surface and
outside-container witnesses fail before the correct subject appears; diagnostics
stay payload-free, no focus/actions occur, exact affected unit rows pass and
changed helper consumers receive targeted qualification. S-091 follows S-090;
A-harness.browser and S-064 depend on closure. No change has started.

### S-090 implementation entry — privileged path normalization

control transport; Sections 12.2–12.2.2 and REQ-450/451/460 govern owned test-route
credentials and runtime/clock controls. The current helper's namespace check is
an explicit engineering enforcement of that boundary. No new product requirement
or owner amendment is necessary.

empty/traversing/encoded-separator/control-character/fragment or malformed paths,
and preserve valid query bytes. Decode path segments only for rejection; never

private token and envelope behavior. Extend the existing negative matrix and use
the adopted POST clock/set example in the valid request witness. Exact transport
row plus the directly affected identity/owner-characterization row and types are
sufficient; valid request bytes are exercised without changing the server or
clock semantics. No routing/title/schema/profile change is planned.

requested subject. No product-owner amendment is needed. Return no rows for an
absent selected surface; readiness itself requires that surface to be mounted even
when zero rows are expected. Observe shell, controls and rows in a single bounded
poll inside the supplied container, returning the grid from that observation.

mismatch. Explicit editor lookup must also fail on absent surface before actions.

### A-harness.browser clock caller follow-through

### F-083 / S-092 — Strict admission for clock-control JSON

S-091 is closed. Follow-through from browser clock cleanup confirms a separate
implementation gap in `internal/platform/httpapi/testclock.go`, owned in routing
by platform.httpruntime and governed by Harness REQ-461/462. Reset decodes into
`struct{}`, so JSON null is accepted as an empty body. Set decodes case-insensitive
struct fields and treats explicit null command members as absent, allowing an
unknown-cased member or both command members when one is null. Both use a limited
reader whose artificial EOF can hide trailing bytes beyond the limit. Existing
negative matrices omit these boundaries. These are adopted-contract conflicts,
not new specification defects or a reason to alter the clock model.

Remediation: one clock-local bounded body admission path, detecting oversize input
before interpreting EOF and using the existing strict object decoder; reset admits
only an actually empty body or an empty object, set admits exactly one canonical
command member with its non-null typed value. Keep authorization ahead of payload
admission and all clock mutation after admission. Do not create a new JSON framework
or change unrelated public route decoding. Extend existing tests with null/scalar/
array/unknown-case/both-null-member/duplicate/trailing/oversize inputs and prove
fixed-clock preservation on every rejection; keep empty/object reset positives.

Areas: implementation, tests and tracker documentation. Benefit: the privileged
clock control has a closed, bounded, predictable command language using the shared
parser. Compatibility: only invalid test-route inputs are rejected; supported
browser callers and public product APIs/data remain unchanged, without aliases.
Risk if unresolved: malformed commands can unexpectedly reset security-sensitive
harness time or silently bypass the claimed command grammar. Entry gates: adopted
REQ-460–464 read, backend/tooling instructions loaded, S-091 checkpoint closed.
Exit: exact platform.httpruntime clock row demonstrates rejected input never mutates
state, supported set/reset/state behavior survives, formatting and documentation
checks pass. No routing change is needed for added subtests. A-harness.browser,
future A-platform.httpruntime and S-064 depend on this corrective checkpoint.

body or an empty object; null, whitespace-only, non-object and trailing input fail.
Duplicate keys are rejected by the shared parser. Authorization still precedes

### F-085 / S-094 — Require the blocked-retry observation to occur (queued)

The backoff-cancellation test checks `RetryBlockedByContext` only inside an observer
conditional. If the blocked event is never emitted, that assertion never runs.
Other assertions preserve the returned cause and attempt count but do not establish
the observer contract. Remediate by collecting the blocked events and requiring
exactly one with the expected context cause, attempt, status and retry flags.
Retain original failure/cancellation and no-extra-attempt checks.

change planned. Purpose: deterministic observer evidence must report why retry
stopped; no specification amendment is needed for the existing callback contract.

observability could disappear while the return-value tests remain green. Entry:
S-093 checkpoint must close first. Exit: exact existing testcontainersx row passes
with a nonvacuous event assertion, formatting and documentation checks pass.

### F-086 / S-095 — Settle catalog-test resources after early failure (IN PROGRESS)

The concurrent catalog integration test releases its held mutation and deletes
its created databases only on the successful tail. An earlier fatal assertion can
leave its goroutine waiting indefinitely and skip cleanup. Its active-database
companion registers pool cleanup only after all four acquisitions, allowing an
earlier setup failure to strand already-opened handles. These are test-fixture
lifetime defects, not a product specification change.

Remediation: register each pool immediately; give concurrent catalog work bounded
cancellable ownership, release and join every started worker during cleanup, and
clean only targets whose successful CREATE proved ownership. Preserve all existing
exclusion, overlap, cancellation and active-connection assertions. Scope: tests and
this documentation; no public API, selector or data migration. This removes
failure-path contamination and unbounded workers without broadening cleanup
rights or building a general fixture framework. Leaving it unresolved makes a
failed test itself consume shared capacity and obscure subsequent diagnostics.

### F-093 / S-102 — Establish the renderer waiter before asserting it is blocked (queued)

The `six_slots_and_waiting_seventh` case signals `started` before calling reserve,
then uses a nonblocking result read. The assertion can pass before reservation has
run. Cancellation afterward may hide an incorrectly admitted seventh borrower.
Harness REQ-803 bounds provisional slots and REQ-804 allows only one borrower per
slot. This is an ineffective concurrency witness, not a product-specification gap.

Place this service-free subtest in a virtual-time concurrency bubble and wait for
all work to block or finish before checking the seventh result. Keep exact six
slot identities, cancellation cause and released-slot reuse assertions; ensure
cancellation is registered before launching the worker. Scope: tests and tracker;
existing row/profile and production mechanics remain unchanged. Benefit: the
capacity invariant is observed after actual admission, without scheduler delay or
timing thresholds. Leaving it unresolved permits a false pass for over-admission.

without awaiting close in its finally block and leaves its watchdog outside that
cleanup scope. The deliberate unanchored-descendant case signals its exact child
but does not await final pipe closure. Harness fixture cleanup and process-settlement
requirements govern these test-owned resources.

explicit expected failure assertions, and require observed closure. Retain the
special descendant's independent ownership and await its final close. Keep the
Playwright child completion/watchdog within finally, settle before scratch removal,
and avoid signaling an already closed child group. Areas: tests/tracker. Benefit:
failed assertions cannot leave workers, timers or scratch races behind. No production,
selector, profile or compatibility change. Unresolved risk: leaked processes and

selection passes, format/Markdown/whitespace pass. This is not a browser rendering

### F-108 / S-117 — Require one native Playwright result per selected identity (DONE)

The adapter counts matching specs but accepts multiple native results inside one
test, taking the last status; it also falls back from an absent native result to
aggregate expected/unexpected status. A failed then passed retry can therefore
close a selected row as passing. Harness Section 6 Playwright accounting explicitly
requires zero/multiple observations to fail accounting while preserving a product
assertion failure. This is an adopted implementation conflict, not a new retry
policy.

Require one native result for every executed identity. Retain observed product
failures when rejecting invalid cardinality, instead of hiding earlier failures or
promoting aggregate status into an observation. Add independent zero-result,
multiple-pass, failed-then-passed and retry-order controls to the existing adapter
case; preserve settled siblings and invocation cleanup distinctions. Areas:
implementation/tests/tracker. Benefit: row closure proves exact execution with one
clear observation boundary. Compatibility: incomplete/retried native reports reject;
no report translation, selector aliases or product migration. Unresolved risk:
false passing evidence after retries or absent execution. Entry: S-116 closed;
exit: targeted reproduction, exact adapter selection and affected reporter consumers
pass with unchanged single-result behavior. A-harness.browser/S-064 depend on both
corrections; remaining source review is still open.

product requirement. The S-121 lifecycle composition already expresses the required
browser-before-capacity and independent-origin ordering.

fixture cleanup composition, including the presentation viewer, and migrate its
lifecycle callers. Own handles before startup; install cleanup before fallible
setup; attempt independent closures and retain scratch on unresolved cleanup.

scratch after settled work is sufficient for ordinary store fixtures; retain the
explicit close/accounting tests. No blanket fixture rewrite is warranted.

origin cleanup failure. Compatibility: private helper only; selectors, production

### S-151 — Opaque shell command lifetime handles (DONE)

Entry: S-150/E-134 is closed. F-141: the shell maps native capabilities by numeric
PID and clears a cached result when that number is acquired again. A retained old
caller value can consequently select a later command after PID reuse. The native
proof would correctly identify the later command; it cannot repair this earlier
caller-lookup ambiguity. TH-HARNESS-REQ-853 requires exact lifetime ownership.

Remediation: make the freshly allocated opaque capability the sole private shell
control identity. Key owners/results by that handle; expose PID only as an
observation for port/public fixture projections. Migrate all dev, browser child,
artifact, lifecycle and output-capture callers together. Retire old private helper
names without aliases. Journaled browser services keep their recorded proof and
public PID projection; remove the unused unjournaled service fallback instead of
adding a PID-to-handle compatibility bridge. Native controller protocol stays
unchanged. Areas: implementation, tests, documentation; no product specification,
public Make selection, stored data, or schema migration.

Rationale/benefit: control identity describes one acquisition for its entire
lifetime, independent of kernel PID reuse. It reduces state coupling and permits
future callers to retain completed handles safely. Leaving the gap unresolved can
settle a newer owned command when an old caller repeats cleanup. Migration risk:
callers that use a returned value as a port-owner PID must explicitly request the
observation. Trace every helper reference and all artifact-fixture consumers.

Validation/exit: deterministic two-capability/same-observed-PID fixture proves a
retired handle cannot control the newer command; unknown/numeric handles fail
closed, repeated stop and original exit remain intact. Existing real descendant,
acquisition cancellation, dev signals, browser port transfer, artifact and output
capture observations survive. Qualify exact lifecycle rows, affected output-capture
row and shell lint; reuse S-150 native protocol evidence. Browser service/journal
selectors and profiles remain unchanged; use real physical qualification if the
actual journal path changes. No generated inputs are planned. Update this tracker
and close E-135 before resuming the current owner audit. S-064 depends on S-151.

Entry: S-151/E-135 closed. F-142: stop_backend_for_reset still sends raw negative-PID
TERM before polling journal/native liveness. Its read-before-signal sequence is not
an exact signaling authority and duplicates native settlement policy. TH-HARNESS-
REQ-853 and Section12 browser-reset ordering require proved backend termination
before database reset while preserving the declared graceful-drain deadline.

Remediation: expose a private native graceful-drain operation over exact process
proof, sharing identity discovery, pidfd signaling and absence acknowledgement with
ordinary settlement. Cooperative drain never escalates to KILL; timeout remains a
failure for the reset owner, which retains its existing quarantine/cleanup path.
Resolve only an active recorded browser-service launch; close its journal ticket
only after drain succeeds. The shell delegates its existing drain deadline and
checks listener release after native settlement; it neither sends a signal nor
infers process settlement from listener disappearance. No timeout increase or new
retry. Areas: native/Node/shell implementation, targeted tests and this tracker;
no product specification, public selector or storage change is proposed.

Benefit: one reusable ownership check controls reset signaling; future process
lifetime changes cannot leave a second shell policy behind. Unresolved risk is
signaling a reused group or accepting an incomplete drain. Migration is internal
private-protocol/caller only. Retain exact reset failure precedence, backend
generation, traffic drain, borrowed ownership and recovery observations.

### S-153 — Native command workspace-admission inheritance (DONE)

Entry: S-152/E-136 closed. F-143: the private native command supervisor inherits
workspace descriptor9 but does not project it into its workload's exec.Cmd.
Consequently a managed descendant cannot recognize inherited admission and a nested
Make command can try to reacquire admission. The supervisor still holds its own
lease; do not misstate this as proven loss of the outer lease or a product defect.
This is the documented engineering contract of harnessadmission.InheritWorkspace
and workspace/child-process.mjs, downstream of retained ownership in REQ-853.

Remediation: invoke the existing native inheritance helper at the owned-command
launch boundary, preserve descriptor3–8 reservations, close only temporary duplicates,
and fail acquisition before workload launch if projection fails. No new lock owner,
release path, or private admission implementation. Areas: implementation, lifecycle
regression and documentation. Benefit: nested commands use one admitted lifetime;
future native-owned adapters can reuse the same launch boundary. Unresolved risk is
nested admission divergence or avoidable blocking, not a measured performance claim.
No public API, selector or data migration is required.

Exit: a separately scoped real shared lock is installed as descriptor9 for the
fixture parent; its native-owned workload must observe the same device/inode and
read-lock identity. The original fixture parent's descriptor is restored on scope
exit. Existing native protocol and lifecycle tests pass; shell lint and Go formatting
cover the changes. Native inheritance semantics are reused rather than reimplemented.
No generated input or specification amendment is needed. Close E-137 before beginning

The migration established a necessary acquisition distinction: an explicit native failure
before command.Process exists proves no workload was acquired. Such a fact may close a
pending ticket and release capture allocation. A post-launch proof/cleanup failure, including
one before ready publication, must remain unresolved. The native cause projection now
separates those cases; Node never infers absence solely from missing ready/child-close.

spawn, preventing null/string coercion into an unintended executable. This is one result
shape for private adapter failures, not a compatibility alias.

### S-172 entry and implementation decision

S-171/E-155 closed. REQ-603 already requires bounded capture and primary/cleanup
separation, so this repairs an implementation conflict without inventing a product
requirement. Use one native aggregate byte budget across stdout/stderr, default and
maximum256MiB per invocation. This is an internal resource limit, not a performance
contract or timeout. Private callers may request a smaller positive bound. A streaming
writer writes only admitted bytes, reports limit/I/O failure, and wakes the existing
process owner; it never gives the workload the capture-file descriptors. The owner
waits for registration, settles the complete group, joins output workers, then publishes
closed capture-failure facts. Keep generic ignored/inherited command output unchanged.
Capture failure remains primary when settlement also fails; unresolved ownership keeps
private files and journal entries. No parser may consume a truncated success result.
Native and adapter tests use small limits for exact/+1/concurrent/descendant cases,
plus real caller qualification. No full browser portfolio or new public target implied.
E-156 closes this slice and the reopened browser dependency only after targeted evidence.

### S-184 entry contract and assertion plan

Areas: primary Harness §4.2, package producer/consumer, narrow package-archive helper,
its independent file fixtures, authored exact-row backings and generated projections.
Adopt64GiB per package archive/payload file as a generous bounded engineering limit,
not a performance promise. Stream exact owned no-link regular-file bytes; reject
unsafe writes, hardlinks and mutation during acquisition. Publish complete0600 archive
bytes atomically without replacing a prior content-name winner. A duplicate is accepted
only after securely checking equal bytes; differing bytes fail with winner unchanged.

Keep existing content names and archive format. New archive cache is0700. The exact
preexisting owned0755 cache leaf may be tightened by descriptor to0700; no ancestor,
unowned, linked or other-permission directory is repaired. Previously published safe
0644 archives remain readable without in-place rewriting. This removes accidental
public cache access; distributable payload modes remain unchanged. No copying from a
legacy fallback namespace. Owned verified0600 snapshots in unique0700 cache workspaces
are the only archive inputs passed to extraction, and are always cleaned; primary
failure survives cleanup failure. Checksums still prove identity, not authenticity.

Exit assertions: real bytes survive source-path replacement after snapshot; corruption,
linked/nonregular/oversize/change-during-read inputs fail before extraction; racing
same/different publication winners remain intact; failure leaves no publishing temp;
private modes and constrained legacy-cache migration; success/failure/cleanup-only
and combined failure disposal. Qualify existing package-readiness exact row, generated
and catalog (routing backings); schema check only if structured schema changes occur.
No whole package/Docker qualification needed for these deterministic filesystem changes.
S-064 stays dependent on this slice and all remaining owner work.

### S-193 detailed entry decisions

Use one package-owned `package_deployment` resource kind with separate identities for
source/destination containers, volumes and networks, plus a shared workspace/helper.
Proofs bind daemon, minted UUID token and closed scope/family; workspace proof also binds
the immutable helper image and exact native private allocation path. Native admission
validates that path against this runtime's ordinary package-qualification namespace.
S-192 lookup admits the opaque stored proof before private physical cleanup. No caller
path can select an operator directory or another runtime's workspace.

Reserve both minted project namespaces and helper name only after successful observations
prove them absent, including unlabelled colliding names. Register all independent resource
proofs before side effects; explicit container dependencies retain its volumes, network
and workspace until it stops. Query only the reserved project labels for cleanup, inspect
each returned exact identity/label before removal, and verify absence. Bound each listing
to128 resources and each native family attempt to the existing managed-deployment120s
budget; this is a new resource policy, not an increase to an existing test deadline.
Malformed, ambiguous, wrong-daemon or ownership observations fail closed. Sibling attempts
continue; unsafe parents remain pending. Normal allocation teardown follows the same
explicit dependency order qualified against native recovery.

Mutable work is native private detail. Workspace repair may need the shipped immutable
helper image for container-created UID-owned files. Its separately reserved helper name
and exact allocation/run/lease labels remain owned by the workspace proof before create;
lost replies and interrupted repair must not strand an unowned helper. Stop/verify this
helper independently, repair only the native-admitted workspace, and record release only
after helper and workspace absence. Missing workspace is not proof of helper absence.
Ordinary physical workers use the existing owned-process/capture boundary with explicit
resource dependency and policy deadline; recovery uses the existing native physical owner.
No new scheduler, arbitrary cleanup command, global sweep, or broad proof-directory retention.

Qualify pure provider-boundary cases and actual native journal/ordinary/recovery paths,
including blocked parents, partial admission, helper interruption and unrelated survivors.
Keep legacy shell callers/tests intact during S-193. Their migration and retirement remain
S-194. Any design constraint found during implementation must be reconciled here and in
the primary Harness owner before downstream changes, not hidden as a tactical exception.

Runtime failure diagnosis: the S-191 fixture assumes payload readiness follows journal
adoption. `servePipeCommand` actually starts and physically owns the payload before the

receipt after construction or through a returned payload. Areas: implementation,
tests/docs; Core 01 original committed receipt semantics and the existing opaque
result ownership purpose govern. No substantive requirement amendment.

Remediation: recursively copy the row's JSON object/array containers at both existing
copy boundaries, preserving scalar types and wire shape. Keep this helper local to
stored receipts; do not broaden conflict helpers or introduce a shared framework.
Extend the existing idempotency test with real nested cells, independent expected
values, input/output mutation checks and all four result constructors, including the
typed collection-item representation emitted before serialization. Benefit: stable
receipt values and explicit ownership without serialization/coercion. Compatibility:
no durable bytes or selector/profile changes; callers lose accidental shared mutation.
Unresolved risk: a consumer can silently corrupt another consumer's replay value.

integration consumers pass, with format/docs, scan and cleanup recorded. E-209 reserved;
owner and S-064 remain open.

### S-222 / F-207 — Note association paging over eligible counterparts (IN PROGRESS)

`NoteAssociations.List` computes has-more and truncates raw links before checking
counterpart visibility/type/subtype. Multiple deleted or ineligible counterparts can
produce a first page with zero matching items and has-more true, conflicting with
Core 01 REQ-01-242 and REQ-01-675. This is an implementation/test gap against adopted
requirements; no specification change. Areas: implementation/tests/docs.

Remediation: keep Links' bounded canonical keyset lookup and Artifacts' eligibility
ownership. Scan bounded link windows until the requested number of eligible items
and one eligible lookahead are found, or the source is exhausted. Advance scan state
through excluded facts, but bind returned continuation to the last returned eligible
link. Retain current authorization, stable Note version, ordering and transaction
cleanup. Do not add Artifact subtype knowledge to Links or materialize all links.
Benefit: truthful continuation and predictable page membership with cohesive ownership.
Compatibility: corrected page contents/has-more for previously filtered windows; cursor
format and ordering remain valid, no data migration or legacy mode. Unresolved risks:
empty nonterminal pages, misleading terminal controls and unnecessary round trips.

Validation: extend existing association integration with interleaved eligible/deleted/

### S-225 / F-210 — observe Assessment assessor lock contention (IN PROGRESS)

Areas: tests/documentation. The membership contract's helper waits 100 milliseconds
without seeing completion, then assumes the validator blocked membership removal or
user deactivation. Scheduling delay can satisfy this oracle without contention.
The adopted assessor membership/active-user requirement needs a real transaction
boundary witness. Replace elapsed absence with two identified transactions and
PostgreSQL's explicit blocker relation: the mutation transaction must be waiting
on the exact validation transaction before release, then complete and commit after
release. Register bounded rollback/cancellation and worker settlement on failure.
Keep both concrete mutation cases and all membership/default/replay/no-effects cases.

Benefit: causal concurrency assurance independent of machine scheduling; no timing
threshold becomes a product contract. No production/API/schema/routing/profile change.
Risk if unresolved: an ineffective validator lock could appear covered. Exit: exact

### S-242 / F-227 — serialize enterprise-binding receipt admission (DONE)

Areas: implementation/tests/docs; adopted REQ-01-538–540 already requires original
success replay before fresh version/binding checks. All three store operations read
receipts before starting their mutation transaction. Two requests can both miss;
the second then observes a changed user/binding or unique receipt conflict. The
same-subject rotation branch also lacks serialized admission.

Remediation: begin an explicitly Read Committed transaction, acquire the existing
route-identity transaction lock, then read/compare the receipt in that transaction
before owner guards or effects. Roll back independently of request cancellation.
Keep current actor/target scope and request comparison, all first-write guards and
the original retained response. Avoid a new transaction framework or wire alias.
Add deterministic public-route overlap cases for create, rotate, no-op rotate and
retire, each identical and divergent, using observed database blocking rather than
sleep-based overlap assumptions. Require exact status/payload, one receipt and
expected binding/version/audit/session effects. Retain all existing HTTP assertions.

Benefit: one atomic admission boundary gives stable replay under contention.
Compatibility: competing identical admitted requests now replay; divergent requests
return the required transaction conflict before fresh-state conflicts. No storage,
receipt or API schema migration; coordinated deployment avoids mixed writers with
the old admission gap. Risk if unresolved: inconsistent retries and misleading
conflicts during normal overlap. Entry E-232 closed; exit existing binding HTTP row
passes all old/new cases, plus directly affected SQL boundary checks if required by
the new query placement. Reserve E-233. Local credential/user and account mutation
methods show the same pre-transaction pattern and require separate corrective slices
before owner completion; do not consider them resolved by this binding repair.

Areas: implementation/tests/documentation. Core01REQ512/514 and Core04REQ095 require
current linked identity and fail-closed completion. Completion currently reads a
binding before the user lock, then commits transaction consumption/last-auth before
a second transaction creates its session. Retirement can win between those stages;
a failed session write also leaves partial completion effects. Use one transaction
for current provider/user/binding admission, protocol consumption, last-auth update,
session cap/revocation and insertion. Re-read/lock the binding after the user lock
under Read Committed. Extract only the private session-write body shared by local
and enterprise issuance; remove the now-unused separate provider-session capability.
Generate the session token before store completion, publish cookies/revocations only
after commit. No schema, cookie, route or public-error migration; private ports/callers
migrate together without aliases. Benefit: one auditable commit boundary and consistent
user-first lock ordering. Failure can retry an unconsumed transaction after a storage
fault; rejected identity never leaves a session. Add OIDC/SAML retirement/disablement
interleavings plus injected session-write rollback cases, then qualify both protocol
rows, binding lifecycle and directly affected local issuance. Entry E-242 closed;
exit red evidence, all targeted checks and documentation closure. Reserve E-243.

### S-255 / F-240 — validate current TOTP activation authority atomically (DONE)

Areas: implementation/tests/documentation. Core01REQ522/526 require a valid current
auth scope and atomic consumption/activation. Activation currently locks pending
setup before the user, contrary to administrative reset's user-first ordering, and
never rechecks bootstrap supersession/consumption/expiry or session revocation under
its transaction. Lock user, then current auth scope, then pending enrollment under
Read Committed; reject inactive accounts and invalidated authority before any write.
Preserve exact pending-envelope revalidation, replacement revocation and audit atomicity.
Use private typed scope errors mapped to existing public rejection families and
bounded independent rollback. No public field, schema or data migration. Benefit:
clear shared serialization with resets/issuance; no stale authority or lock inversion.
Unresolved risk: superseded bootstrap or revoked session can activate a factor, and
opposed lock ordering can deadlock reset/completion. Qualify both auth modes with
observed mutation barriers, exact reasons/no effects and concurrent single activation,
plus existing lifecycle/secret-envelope and unit coverage. Entry E-245 closed; exit
all targeted checks and documentation closure. Reserve E-246. Begin replay semantics
and begin admission remain separate pending work; no normative change inferred here.

### S-255 completion checkpoint / E-246

Activation now locks user→auth scope→pending enrollment under Read Committed,
checks current activity and scope identity/state, then preserves the existing exact
envelope check and atomic activation/consumption/revocation/audit. Typed private
bootstrap failures preserve expired/consumed/superseded reasons; absent, inactive,
revoked or expired session authority fails401/session_required. No new wire vocabulary,
data migration or assertion retirement. The caller uses locked current user state for
activation audit, rather than the earlier request snapshot.

Ten public-route barrier cases are attached to the existing credential lifecycle row:
three invalidated bootstrap states, two inactive-account modes, revoked/expired session,
reset deleting pending setup, and two simultaneous-completion modes. They prove exact
error/status/reasons, no rejected factor/pending-consumption/audit/version/cookie/session
effects, exactly one concurrent activation and correct non-revoking first enrollment.
The reset case also exercises user-first pending deletion without lock inversion.
Existing replacement, envelope substitution and protocol cases retain their assertions.

### S-256 / F-241 — define TOTP begin replay intent in its primary owner (DONE)

Areas: specification/documentation. Core01REQ525 says same normalized request while
its table and AC336 describe auth-scope/key replay, without defining whether transient
password/TOTP proofs are replay identity. A request merely asks to create one pending
setup; it supplies no mutable business payload beyond its key. Adopt scope/key intent:
proof fields authorize fresh creation only, structural validation and current auth-scope
validity still precede replay, and a matching live pending enrollment returns its exact
seed without retaining/rechecking old proof values. Different key/scope conflicts while
pending; overlapping matching requests produce one pending enrollment/audit. Fresh
replacement must still verify current password/factor against current state at admission.
This deliberately avoids a new secret-derived receipt column, migration, historical
hash version or requirement to replay a now-expired TOTP code. No new product feature.
Compatibility: formalizes scope/key replay already exposed by current implementation,
but makes current-authority and concurrent admission obligations explicit. A client
cannot use another auth scope to retrieve the seed. Risk unresolved: incompatible
or secret-retaining implementations inferred from ambiguous wording, and unsafe replay
shortcuts. Entry E-246 closed; exit manual consistency review of primary requirement,
route tables and AC336, Markdown/diff checks; S-257 must implement the admission repair
against this adopted owner before Auth closure. Reserve E-247; documentation-only slice.

### S-257 / F-242 — serialize TOTP begin creation and replay (DONE)

Areas: implementation/tests/documentation. Implement Core01REQ525 as adopted in E-247.
The current early replay releases seed material without transactional current-authority
validation; fresh begin lacks a stable user lock, so concurrent identical empty-set
requests can conflict instead of replaying. It trusts earlier replacement-proof state.
Use one user→auth-scope→pending admission boundary for both creation and replay. Pass a
small private scope/input plus optional freshly authorized creation; absence means
replay only and can never create setup. Derive replacement state from current locked
user data and check that fresh proof was verified against that same credential state.
Always derive the response seed from the admitted stored enrollment. Remove the early
seed-response branch, unused replay flag and excess private positional arguments;
migrate all callers/stubs together. No schema, data or public selector migration.
Benefit: explicit intent and creation authority, one replay boundary, no secret-derived
receipt history. Risk unresolved: stale authority leaks seed or creates setup, matching
concurrency fails spuriously, or replacement uses invalidated proof. Validation: exact
fresh/replay overlaps, stale session/bootstrap and credential transitions, proof-free
same-scope replay with identical seed, changed-key/scope rejection, exactly one begin
audit and no rejection effects; existing unit/lifecycle/envelope cases preserved.
Entry E-247 owner amendment and docs closed; exit targeted checks, routing accounting
and docs closure. Reserve E-248; A-module.auth/S-064 remain open.

argument port and now-unused callStub9Result2 are removed. All four test stubs and
service callers migrate together. Existing identity/scope/time/factor-state assertions

session/bootstrap authority invalidations, and three replacement-proof paths. Positive

### S-271 / F-256 — sequence-safe live tailing across clock changes (IN PROGRESS)

Areas: implementation/tests/documentation, module.collaboration. REQ-01-271 makes
per-incident stream sequence authoritative. Global ordering by raw emission time
can deliver a later sequence first, advance the tail cursor and permanently skip
earlier events across a batch boundary. Order pending events by their per-incident
cumulative maximum emission time, then incident and sequence. This preserves
chronological interleaving while never allowing a later sequence to overtake an
earlier one; no cross-incident causal order or fairness guarantee is invented.
Extend the existing durable-store row with reversed-clock messages spanning the
100-message batch and an independent incident. Verify exact sequence and event
identity across pages and terminal exhaustion. No public API/schema migration;
previously skipped live events remain recoverable through retained replay where
available. Risk unresolved: live clients miss committed changes. Entry E-262 closed;
exit exact affected row passes, scans/cleanup and documentation recorded. E-263 reserved.

### S-274 / F-259 — complete snapshot replay without whole-range buffering (IN PROGRESS)

Areas: implementation/tests/documentation, module.collaboration. REQ-01-273/274 require
covered retained ranges to replay in order and missing ranges to reset without partial
replay. The store currently accepts interior/terminal holes and resets valid retained
ranges above10000 events or16 MiB. Replace whole-range buffering with an owned read-only
repeatable-read replay snapshot: validate token/high-water, prove complete consecutive
range, prevalidate canonical events in bounded pages, then emit from the same snapshot
through a bounded-page visitor. Explicit disposal and context cancellation release
the snapshot. The route acknowledges only the prepared outcome and sends a fresh
presence snapshot after successful replay. Migrate all internal callers together;
remove obsolete result slice and caps without aliases. No schema/wire/data migration.
Benefit: consistent retention/replay semantics and memory proportional to one page;
unresolved risk is silently incomplete synchronization or unnecessary full reloads.

pruning during a prepared replay, cancellation/visitor failure/disposal, and existing
socket resume/handshake behavior. Record exact targeted evidence and docs. E-266 reserved.

### S-274 completion checkpoint / E-266

S-274/F-259 DONE. `PreparedReplay` owns a read-only repeatable-read transaction.

issues its replacement token before taking the snapshot connection, bounds initial
replay by the existing45-second heartbeat lifetime, and sends fresh presence afterward.

presence removal on close. Current establishment consumes replay before observing

### S-292 / F-277 entry: retire migration sessions after uncertain lock cleanup

F-277 must_fix: failed detached unlock returns a safe error but both the owner and
pinned Goose provider then call sql.Conn.Close, which returns the physical session
to the pool. It does not itself release a session advisory lock. A failed/panicking
unlock can therefore leave a locked pooled session and obscure a primary failure.
Local pinned database/sql and Goose source confirms this path. REQ-01-657 requires
bounded release and primary-failure precedence; borrowed pool lifetime stays separate.

Remediation: normalize lock/unlock panics without private text and retire an uncertain
physical session through database/sql's supported ErrBadConn discard boundary.
Retain the borrowed pool and primary error. Add a small local connector fixture that
observes physical Close, replacement connection acquisition and lock state, alongside
plain failure/panic/timeout and successful reuse cases. Areas implementation/tests/docs;
no public API/data migration or new driver dependency. Benefit: a failed cleanup cannot
return a lock-bearing session for reuse. Risk if unresolved: stalled migrations and
misleading error precedence. Entry S-291 closed; reserve E-287. Exit exact locker units
and actual apply/crypto-admission integration rows pass, with docs closure. Do not
claim injected real-network unlock failures or full migration-suite acceptance.
