### S-299 / F-284 entry: settle entity concurrency and failed import fixtures

F-284 must_fix test-lifecycle gap: concurrent claim requests invoke fatal test helpers
inside worker goroutines. A transport failure can exit a worker before sending its
response, leaving the parent waiting forever; an early parent assertion can leave
another response unclosed. The portability failure helper installs no rollback guard
before its failure assertion, so an unexpected result bypasses nested-transaction
cleanup. These are fixture engineering obligations, not new product requirements.
Remediation: construct requests in the parent; collect every worker's response/error,
join all workers before assertions, bound/cancel request lifetime and register response
cleanup before checking results. Install immediate rollback guards for import probes
and preserve rollback errors. Areas tests/docs only; existing rows/profiles, concurrency
and SQL isolation remain. Benefit: failures stay diagnosable without stranded work or
transactions. Risk unresolved: hangs/resource leakage can obscure actual regressions.
Reserve E-295; entry S-298 closed. Exit exact claim-concurrency and import-invariant
rows pass and documentation checkpoint closes. No general fixture framework or runtime
product change is introduced.

the bounded manifest and remove the redundant single-caller helper. No whole

token algorithm is unchanged.

### S-551 / F-536 / E-552 — Committed change-set chronology

Recorded before editing; allocation verified. IN_PROGRESS. E-361 review found
`ensureNoLaterRollbackTargetMutationTx` uses `created_at` and only recognizes
equal-time successors inside the selected change set. Different change sets at
the same timestamp, or later commits with an earlier clock, escape the guard.
A complete non-row value can recur after an inverse, so value equality cannot
establish that the selected action remains latest. Core01 REQ-01-107 requires
later committed same-target changes to reject isolated reversal.

implementation. A Revisions-owned transactional allocator serializes assignment,
imports preserve admitted orders and advance the allocator, and rollback uses
that order plus mutation sequence. Existing history display/cursor timestamp
ordering is a separate contract and remains unchanged. Do not infer chronology
from UUIDs or retrofit ambiguous preexisting history; schema migration must
refuse populated old history. Validate portable order scalar/uniqueness, exact
source/export preservation, imported successor allocation, transactional rollback
and concurrency, plus public rollback behavior. Separate row-chain order and

### S-559 / F-544 / E-560 — Canonical row identity for rollback currentness

Recorded before editing; allocation verified. IN_PROGRESS. Generic record and
source-specific row target kinds can address the same physical record through
the admitted catalog (S-554 preserves this intentional behavior). Currentness
still queries exact target_kind/target_id strings. A later admitted mutation
using the other row spelling therefore escapes the committed-order guard.
The coordinator only compares the request base version to current state and
validates retained snapshot shape; it does not compare the selected old after
snapshot to current state before restoring the old before image. This permits
an isolated old reversal to overwrite later work across row target aliases.

### S-593 / F-578 / E-594 — protected Assessment subject admission

Recorded before implementation; identities verified unused (previous occurrence
was a next-unused checkpoint only). IN_PROGRESS. Assessment subject validation
reads Records without locking, then reads Host/Identity active typed eligibility.
Unlike a support target, the subject need not participate in a Link. Concurrent
deletion or merge can therefore invalidate the admitted subject before creation
commits; generic active-Link validation cannot repair this boundary. Source owner
merge protects Records before changing typed state, and keeps merged envelopes
active. Retaining that Records writer lock before re-reading typed eligibility
respects its existing lock order and avoids a shared-to-writer upgrade if a subject
also appears among support refs.

### S-601 / F-586 / E-602 closure — ordered entity Party assignments

CLOSED and targeted-qualified. HostIdentity protects the complete addition set
through Links before effects, then executes each validated action through Links in
request order. It retains each actual record_link mutation in that order. A removal
then addition tombstones the original Link and creates a distinct active identity;
a missing first removal fails even if a later action would add the membership.

ordinary receipt/history/publication ownership and atomic rollback. Existing
Links set operations and their other callers are unchanged; no compatibility
wrapper or new public wire shape was introduced. Core01REQ069/327a already govern.

### S-624 / F-609 / E-625 — Merge claim preparation drift

Recorded before editing; identities verified unused. IN_PROGRESS. Core02
REQ-02-066 requires a complete normalized claim lock set before Merge effects.
PrepareIdentifierClaimsTx reads both source tuple sets before acquiring their
advisory locks; Merge never revalidates that prepared set after envelope/source
admission. A writer holding the old claim can commit changed identifiers while
Merge waits. A request whose base versions match the newly committed source can
then pass version checks and reach effects with an incomplete claim lock set.
Existing mismatch tests do not exclude this case, and later trigger locking is
too late to preserve the complete-set preparation order.

Adopt explicit normalized-set drift rejection in primary Core02 before production
changes. Carry an opaque source-owned preparation containing the normalized tuple
union and source identities; re-read/compare that union after destructive source
and version admission, before prepared collision disclosure or effects. Reuse
`merge_precondition_failed/protected_set_changed`; never acquire new tuple locks
under held source locks. Keep missing/locked/version precedence and complete
third-record collision checks. No compatibility alias for the single private
application consumer is needed.

Add deterministic public Merge witnesses for Host/Identity and each participant:
hold a real source update and its claim locks, observe Merge blocked on that
transaction, commit the update, require exact set-drift rejection with independently
captured expected state/no effects, then same-request success/replay from a freshly
prepared set. Fixtures explicitly exercise admission, not complete portable
history. Retain existing version/collision/protected-set assertions. Qualify the
existing Merge HTTP and store roots and actual boundary; no new root, catalog row,
profile, generated output, browser or measurement work. Close S-624 checks before

Handoff contract:

- Go discovery is exhaustive independently of bounded evaluation. Located private
  records require explicit dispositions; malformed/legacy responses fail. Native
  execution uses declared identity/signatures and exact arguments, with no
  receiver-name or permissive unknown-method fallback.
- Runtime constructors and inspection share the pure lexical validator. Closed
  templates reject comments, unsafe holes and unterminated/unsupported tokens;
  quoted data, parameters and complete-token composition remain supported.
- The [enforcement guide](../guides/sql-ownership-enforcement.md) documents native
  API dispositions, pinned-inventory review, how to add providers/shared readers,
  exact package/declaration authority, rejected examples and maintenance limits.
- Reference Data callbacks carry immutable domain entries until local batch
  construction. Private test-support adapters take sealed queries/statements.
  No opaque-batch or raw-forwarding compatibility exception was introduced.
- Adopt the private analysis response and callers atomically. There is no public
  API, schema, stored-data or deployment migration. Records locking, source read
  separation, package grants and browser-to-HTTP assertions are retained.
- Deliberate limits remain: finite construction, no arbitrary heap/call-graph
  inference, explicit foreign-library boundaries, immutable local prepared/batch
  provenance, and rejection of unqualified stateful/raw-protocol execution.
  New uses require qualification; they must not inherit broader authority.

  atomic private-interface migrations remain documented above. There is no public
